Msg: Online quizzes, competitions, and free tools that ask for your email, phone number, or personal details are often data harvesting tools. Ask yourself whether the value being offered is worth the information being requested.

Oversharing on social media increases your exposure to targeted attacks. Your job title, workplace, travel schedule, and daily routine are valuable information to social engineers. Be thoughtful about what your public profiles reveal.

That fun quiz asking your childhood nickname, first school, or mother's maiden name is not just entertainment. These are classic password recovery answers and fraudsters design these quizzes deliberately. Think before you participate. Never use your work email to complete them.

Treat personal data like cash; do not share it casually, do not leave it lying around, and always ask why someone needs it before handing it over.

Your BVN is tied to every bank account you own in Nigeria. Never share it over the phone, via WhatsApp, in a form you did not initiate, or with anyone who is not your verified bank. No legitimate bank staff will ever ask for your BVN directly. If someone asks for it, stop immediately.
Your digital identity is as valuable as your financial identity. Treat every piece of personal information with the same care you give your bank card or PIN.

Avoid saving passwords in browser autofill on shared devices. What you save for convenience can be accessed by the next person who uses that device.
Biometrics are helpful but not a complete replacement for good password hygiene. Fingerprints and face recognition can be bypassed. Always have a strong PIN or password as backup.
